summary.text: Republican John Cowan won the election for Georgia's 11th Congressional District on November 3, 2026, defeating Chris Harden according to unofficial results, and is set to take office on January 3, 2027.
A Cartersville native, he is a neurosurgeon who describes himself as a small-business owner and a "conservative outsider."
He ran unsuccessfully for Georgia's 14th District in 2020 and won the June 16, 2026 Republican runoff for the open 11th District seat vacated by Rep. Barry Loudermilk.

paragraphs.text: Cowan's campaign website says his family has been part of the Bartow County community since the 1930s; his father was a physician and his mother a schoolteacher, and he grew up on the family farm and graduated from Cartersville High School.

He graduated from Davidson College with a B.S. in physics, received an M.D. from the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, and completed a neurosurgery residency at the University of Michigan Medical School.
Cowan works as a neurosurgeon and says he has cared for patients for over 20 years. He also describes himself as a small-business owner who has built businesses creating jobs in the district.
As of his 2020 campaign, Ballotpedia listed him as founder of Cortex Toys and Cortex Holdings.
Cowan ran in the 2020 Republican primary for Georgia's 14th District and lost the August 11, 2020 runoff to Marjorie Taylor Greene.
He advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary and won the June 16, 2026 runoff over Rob Adkerson, 65.0% to 35.0%, for the seat vacated by Rep. Barry Loudermilk.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Dr. Anne Cowan, are raising four children and are active in their church, where he serves as an elder.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 55.4% of the vote to Chris Harden's 44.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
